items.descriptionOriginal: Getting your daily steps in may be a little easier if you live in Hoboken, New Jersey. Earlier this month, Architectural Digest released a list of the nine most walkable cities in the U.S. based on recent studies, Redfin’s Walk Score tool, and consultations with realtors, residents, and tourism experts. The 1-square-mile city, which sits just across the Hudson River from downtown Manhattan, earned the top spot due to its ample public transportation and dense street grid. It received a 97 out of 100 on Walk Score, which measures the ability for residents to run errands and access amenities without a car — factors that can go a long way for physical health, mental health, and the health of the planet. View this post on Instagram “[Walkability] can benefit everything from household finances and health to the environment and overall quality of life,” Daryl Fairweather, chief economist at Redfin, told the outlet. She added: “Walkable neighborhoods also create more opportunities for people to interact with local businesses, use public spaces and resources, and connect with their neighbors.” Science backs up those benefits. A 2021 paper showed higher walkability was associated with lower mortality rates in a cohort of 13,832 women. And a 2020 study of over 31,000 adults found that those living in high-walkability areas were 150% more likely to engage in adequate levels of physical activity and 76% less likely to be obese. Additionally, research from 2013 suggested that participants who walked more in their neighborhood experienced improved social interactions and felt more social cohesion within the community. RELATED: How 11,000 Twins Helped Illustrate the Importance of Making Cities Walkable In terms of the planet, Elizabeth Sawin, director of the Multisolving Institute, a research organization focused on climate change, equity, health, well-being, and biodiversity, summed up the power of walkability in a 2024 interview with Grist: “Every trip taken on foot instead of by a fossil fuel-powered car reduces greenhouse gas emissions.” Here’s the full list of America’s most walkable cities from Architectural Digest : 1. Hoboken, New Jersey 2. West Hollywood, California 3. Boston, Massachusetts 4. San Francisco, California 5. New York, New York 6. Washington, D.C. 7. Chicago, Illinois 8. Miami, Florida 9. Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

Ο Αμερικανός εν…
items.descriptionOriginal: Scaling America’s clean energy solutions, Duke Energy Florida has proposed four new utility-scale solar sites with a combined generating capacity of 300 megawatts (MW). The plan to expand the renewable energy portfolio of the Southern state was announced Tuesday, November 10, as electricity demand continues to grow across the state. The American energy company has filed plans with the Florida Public Service Commission (PSC) to construct the four solar facilities, which are expected to enter service by mid-2028. Together, the projects will add 300 MW of emissions-free electricity generation to Florida’s power grid. Four solar sites across Florida The planned facilities include solar energy sites in Orange and Sumter Counties, with a tentative online date of June 2028. The Orange County facilities include Nova Renewable Energy Center, Bull Creek Renewable Energy Center, and Wewahootee Renewable Energy Center. The construction of the former two are expected to begin early next year. Construction for the third is slated to begin in May 2027. Hogeye Renewable Energy Center is the only one planned in the Sumter County. According to Duke Energy Florida, the new projects are part of its long-term strategy to meet rising electricity demand while increasing the share of renewable energy in its generation mix. “Our strategy is centered on delivering cleaner energy while maintaining reliable and affordable service for our customers,” Melissa Seixas, Duke Energy Florida state president, said in a statement. Each facility will generate electricity using photovoltaic solar panels connected to Duke Energy Florida’s transmission network. Once operational, the projects will collectively provide enough renewable generation to strengthen the utility’s growing solar portfolio. However, the company has not yet revealed the individual capacity of the four proposed solar sites. Clean energy expansion The latest filing is part of the company’s plan to expand the state’s battery system to store excess energy when power demand is low. Through these new systems, the company hopes to provide customers with clean solar energy even during the period of no sunlight. “These solar energy sites are just one example of how we’re planning for the future and strengthening our system to continue providing safe, reliable power, at the lowest possible price, for years to come,” Seixas added. Over the next decade, it plans to build over 1 gigawatt of battery storage , the company said in a statement expanding on the long-term impact of the proposed solar utility sites. The utility noted that the four projects are also projected to deliver approximately $1 billion in customer savings over their operating lifetimes through reduced fuel costs, although the primary focus of the proposal is to add new renewable generating capacity to Florida’s electric grid. Beyond providing cost-effective fuel to power the American grid, the new facilities would also provide emission-free energy to the U.S. homes. According to the company, about 1.1 million cubic feet of natural gas, 12,000 barrels of fuel oil, and 9,000 tons of coal are saved annually at each solar energy site. The company currently owns, operates, and maintains 25 solar energy sites that contribute 1,850 MW to the grid. Each energy site holds the capacity to power nearly 15,000 homes, it said .

items.descriptionOriginal: When people daydream about not having to work for a living, they usually envision being super wealthy . They don’t usually imagine living alongside their ancestors thousands of years ago. But the reality is that jobs as we know them (working hours, salaries and paychecks, work-life balance, paid or unpaid time off, overtime, and more) are super recent on the human timeline. Even specialized jobs, which have been around for thousands of years, are still new compared to the roughly 290,000 years of human evolution that preceded anything resembling what we think of as “employment.” How much time did basic survival take? Less than you might think. A YouTube video from Axen explores what humans did all day before they had to work for a living, and it’s quite fascinating. The obvious answer is “survive,” but that didn’t actually fill the whole day. The video points out that modern humans spend about 90,000 hours of their lives working, roughly a third of their waking existence. However, anthropologists have studied pre-agricultural peoples across different continents. The general consensus is that basic survival activities took between 15 and 20 hours per week. That’s a part-time job in terms of hours. What did people do the rest of the time? Whatever they wanted, basically. It might be easy to assume that prehistoric humans were solely focused on not dying, but that doesn’t appear to be the case. Our super ancient ancestors were creative As the video explains, people actually spent time on creative hobbies. Here are a few examples: “In 1994, explorers discovered Chauvet Cave in southern France. Inside were paintings created roughly 30,000 years ago: horses, lions, and rhinoceroses rendered with perspective, shading, and movement. These weren’t crude stick figures. This was sophisticated art that required skill, planning, and, most importantly, time. Someone spent hours, maybe days, deep inside a cave by firelight, painting animals on a wall. Not for survival. Not for food. But for beauty, for meaning, for something to do. Deep in France’s Ardèche Valley, the Chauvet Cave hides a 36,000-year-old secret: some of humanity’s earliest masterpieces. Discovered in 1994, its walls burst with vivid paintings of lions, rhinos, and horses, drawn with charcoal and ochre by Paleolithic artists. These aren’t… pic.twitter.com/AoT80BsHNN — Dreams N Science (@dreamsNscience) May 20, 2025 In Blombos Cave in South Africa, archaeologists found 75,000-year-old perforated shell beads : tiny holes drilled through seashells, clearly meant to be strung together as jewelry. The nearest estuary was 20 km (about 12 miles) away. Someone walked 40 km (about 25 miles) round trip just to collect shells, then spent hours carefully drilling holes with stone tools just to look good. In 2008, researchers found a 40,000-year-old flute carved from a vulture bone in Germany. Five finger holes, perfectly spaced. Whoever made this understood music. They understood pitch. And they spent significant time crafting it. Not for hunting. Not for defense. For music.” What a day in the life might have looked like Axen describes what a typical day might have looked like before jobs: “You wake up around dawn. The fire from last night is still smoldering. Someone adds wood. You eat leftover meat or fish from yesterday. Maybe some nuts or berries collected the day before. Breakfast is social. People talk. They plan loosely for the day. Not because they have to, but because that’s what humans do.” Hunting doesn’t happen every day. You might just stay at camp and build or sharpen tools, weave a basket, or prepare an animal hide. “This isn’t work in the modern sense,” the video points out. “There’s no clock, no supervisor. You do it because competence matters. Because being skilled earns respect. Because making things well is part of being human.” If hunting does take place, it’s a small group that does it. Humans didn’t generally chase down prey. We were persistence hunters, tracking animals for hours until they overheated and collapsed, as demonstrated in this video: That could take three to six hours. “We’re the only species that can do this effectively because we can sweat and regulate our body temperature while running,” the video explains. “Most animals can’t, so we outlast them.” After the animal is carried back, butchered, and eaten, the “work” for the day is basically done. Afternoon and evening are for bonding and leisure For the rest of the day, people rest, socialize, do arts and crafts, and otherwise engage in leisure activities. Conversations during the morning revolve around survival activities, whereas later in the day, they shift. People laugh, joke, and tell stories around the fire. This bonding time is important. Time spent talking around the fire builds culture, as myths and legends are created and passed down. And relationships are key to survival. “In a world without money or police or written contracts, your survival depends entirely on your relationships,” the video explains. “If people don’t like you, they don’t have to share food when you’re hungry. So you invest enormous amounts of time in those bonds. Not because it’s productive. Because it’s how humans stay human.” Early humans spent a lot of time socializing around the fire. Photo credit: Canva Sleep may have looked different, too. Historian Roger Ekirch found evidence that before artificial light, many people in pre-industrial Europe slept in two phases, with about four hours of sleep, an hour or two awake in the dark, and then a second sleep. Was life really better back then? It’s easy to romanticize a daily life that sounds so simple. Community, relationships, art, and less time on the daily grind: all of that sounds great. But simple doesn’t mean easy. What the video doesn’t really touch on are the dangers humans had to deal with more directly than we do now, like wild animals and the elements. Diseases and infections from injuries were a lot scarier in the days before science and modern medicine. And naturally, we couldn’t just transport our soft, sofa-accustomed bodies back into ancient times and find ourselves fully enjoying our leisure time. The physical demands of that life alone would require a huge adjustment. But there’s something we can learn from the lives of our ancient ancestors: Spending time each day on creative pursuits and enjoying time with other people are integral parts of being human. It would be lovely if we could all just work part-time jobs to make a living and have ample free time to spend as we please. Most of us can’t, but perhaps we can use the free time we do have to do more of the things that truly make us human. You can follow Axen on YouTube for other interesting educational videos. This article originally appeared in June. It has been updated. The post What did ancient humans do all day before ‘work’ was invented? It wasn’t all about survival. appeared first on Upworthy .

items.titleOriginal: Woman ticketed for driving with phone in her ‘right hand’ has a huge surprise for police officer
items.description: Η αποσπασμένη οδήγηση είναι ένα επικίνδυνο θέμα που οι αστυνομικοί λαμβάνουν σοβαρά υπόψη. Αλλά όταν η Κέιτι Τόμας, που διευθύνει τη σελίδα των μέσων κοινωνικής δικτύωσης Slightly Off Balance, ανασύρθηκε στη Φλόριντα για την παράβαση, είχε ερωτήσεις. Ο αναπληρωτής του σερίφη της κομητείας Παλμ Μπιτς, γράφοντας την αναφορά, επέμεινε ότι οδηγούσε με το τηλέφωνό της στο δεξί της χέρι. Αυτό δεν έγινε…
items.descriptionOriginal: Distracted driving is a dangerous issue that police officers take seriously. But when Katie Thomas, who runs the social media page Slightly Off Balance , was pulled over in Florida for the offense, she had questions. A Palm Beach County sheriff’s deputy writing the citation insisted that she was driving with her phone in her right hand. That didn’t make sense to her. The woman uploaded a clip of the interaction in which she asks the deputy for clarification. According to the deputy, he witnessed Katie committing the driving infraction. Katie asked for clarification several more times because it would be impossible for her to hold a phone in her right hand. Why? She doesn’t have one . A woman being pulled over. Photo credit: Canva In the video, which has been viewed over 40 million times on TikTok, Katie pokes fun at the situation. “Turns out you can still get a ticket for driving with a device in your right hand, even if you don’t have a right hand,” she says, holding up her arm. Clearly, the entire lower part of her right arm is missing . After cutting to the bizarre interaction between herself and the deputy, Katie shows herself attempting to hold a phone with her nonexistent hand. Spoiler alert: it doesn’t work. In the video, the deputy can be heard saying, “If you want to take it to court, option five on the back of the ticket. That’s how you take it to court.” Taking it to court is exactly what she planned to do. The internet had a field day One person begs, “Please take us to court with you, I want to hear the judge.” Another writes, “I’m glad you recorded him saying it was the right hand otherwise I guarantee he would have lied later on and claim he never said that.” “Ok but how would you be able to drive with a phone in ur LEFT hand anyway,” someone questions. “Oh I wanna see a part 2. I know it sucks tho, cause you shouldn’t have to take time off work/life just to prove a cop wrong,” a person laments. One commenter shares a cheeky way Katie could have handled the situation, writing, “I would have said ‘ok I’ll see you in court’ and waved with your right hand to get his reaction. And then still gone to court to let the judge know he was lying.” Some people wonder why she didn’t tell the deputy on the spot that she didn’t have a right hand. But others argue that the deputy had already proven to be untrustworthy and would likely change his story. Katie didn’t respond to those questions, though some commenters noted that the deputy was standing right at her car window. Katie appears to have a sense of humor limb difference, liking several comments that joke about her missing hand. “I would have held my right hand out for the ticket. So glad you got that admission recorded,” someone writes. “Cutting your hand off to get out of a traffic ticket is wild,” another jokes. No court for Katie As it turns out, the court date never happened. Days before her scheduled hearing, the deputy requested that the citation be dismissed, and on May 27, 2026, Katie confirmed on social media that the case was dropped, citing a lack of evidence. The Palm Beach County Sheriff’s Office later said it dismissed the citation after reviewing state statutes and unclear violation labels in its citation software. In an interview with CBS News , she expressed compassion for the deputy, saying, “I would hope that he gives himself grace for the interaction.” @slightlyoff.balance The finale!!!!! #court #cbs #update ♬ original sound – slightlyoff.balance It’s a strange kind of vindication: no dramatic day in court, just a dismissal and an agency review of the case. Commenters had been gobsmacked from the start that she could be cited for this particular infraction, and plenty stuck around for the payoff. It’s proof that speaking up, and having the video to back it up, can sometimes get results. This article originally appeared in March. It has been updated. The post Woman ticketed for driving with phone in her ‘right hand’ has a huge surprise for police officer appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: Happy Eco News How 326 Fence Construction Helps North Texas Homeowners Create Private, Durable Outdoor Spaces Reading Time: 5 minutes How 326 Fence Construction Helps North Texas Homeowners Create Private, Durable Outdoor Spaces Key Takeaways 326 Fence Construction is based in Nevada, Texas, and serves Collin County and surrounding North Texas communities. Custom wood privacy fencing is a practical option for homeowners who want a more private, enclosed backyard. On-site measurements help account for slopes, gates, existing structures, access, and other site conditions. Fence cost depends on linear footage, materials, height, design, gate needs, and the property’s complexity. Wood fence performance depends on material selection, proper installation, weather exposure, and ongoing maintenance. For homeowners dealing with exposed backyards, aging fence lines, or properties that need clearer boundaries, 326 Fence Construction provides custom residential fencing solutions throughout Nevada, Lavon, Josephine, Farmersville, Princeton, McKinney, and nearby North Texas communities. The company builds wood privacy fences, metal fencing, pipe-and-steel fencing, ranch-style fencing, and custom gates tailored to each property’s use. A new fence should do more than mark a line between neighboring yards. It should support privacy, help define usable outdoor areas, and fit the home’s appearance and practical needs. During a consultation, 326 Fence Construction can review material choices, fence styles, gate options, and custom hardwoods requests based on the project’s budget, maintenance expectations, and layout. Considering these factors early can help homeowners choose a fence that suits their property and long-term plans. A Practical Answer to Backyard Privacy Concerns Many fence projects begin with a straightforward problem. Nearby homes may overlook a yard, an old fence may have loose boards or leaning sections, or a family may want a more defined space for outdoor living. A custom wood privacy fence can create visual separation while giving a backyard a finished, natural look. 326 Fence Construction approaches fencing as a property-specific project rather than a one-size-fits-all installation. Homeowners can discuss whether their priorities are privacy, pet containment, improved curb appeal, a secure gate, or a combination of these goals. The resulting plan can account for the fence line, desired height, style, and transitions around patios, sheds, trees, or changes in elevation. Local Service Throughout Collin County Based in Nevada, Texas, 326 Fence Construction serves homeowners and landowners across Collin County, including Lavon, Josephine, Farmersville, Princeton, and McKinney, as well as surrounding North Texas communities. Local projects can have very different needs, from a compact suburban backyard to a larger property requiring ranch-style fencing and a wider access gate. Planning a fence locally often means looking beyond the visible yard. Property owners may need to consider drainage, slopes, neighborhood or HOA standards, access for installation, existing landscaping, and the location of utilities. The owner-led business is headed by Clayton Dacey, whose background includes service as a police officer and whose company emphasizes clear communication and personal involvement throughout the project. Cedar, Wood, and Custom Material Choices Wood remains a popular fencing material because it provides privacy and design flexibility without losing a natural appearance. Cedar is a common choice for privacy fencing, while treated wood and other suitable materials may also be considered based on the design, budget, and maintenance plan. Important Factors When Choosing Fence Materials Privacy level: Board-on-board and closely spaced picket designs can provide more visual coverage than more open styles. Fence height: Height should support the homeowner’s privacy goals while complying with applicable local or neighborhood requirements. Exposure: Sun, rain, wind, and ground moisture can influence material and construction decisions. Maintenance: Wood fences benefit from periodic inspection, cleaning, and timely repair or refinishing when needed. Appearance: Top caps, trim, stain, and gate details can help a new fence complement the home and landscape. items.descriptionOriginal: Happy Eco News Reducing Waste in Renovation Projects Can Be Easy: Just Apply These 7 Practices Reading Time: 4 minutes Reducing Waste in Renovation Projects Can Be Easy: Just Apply These 7 Practices Renovating your home can leave behind more waste than you might expect. Old cabinets, broken tiles, discarded flooring, leftover paint and piles of packaging can quickly add up. Much of this material ends up in landfills, even though some could have been reused, donated or recycled. However, a few changes in how you plan, shop and manage construction waste can make your renovation more sustainable and keep useful materials in circulation. Here are seven ways to reduce waste in your home renovation projects. 1. Plan Your Renovation Before Buying Materials Your renovation might involve just one room, but the materials you use still contribute to the construction industry’s environmental footprint. The buildings and construction sector contributes to 37% of global emissions and nearly 50% of global material extraction. You can reduce the resources your project consumes, including materials that might otherwise end up unused, by planning your renovation carefully. Before placing orders, measure each room and calculate how much flooring, paint and lumber you’ll need. Ask your contractor to help estimate quantities, accounting for reasonable cutting allowances and possible mistakes. This gives you a better shopping list and helps prevent excessive purchases. Design decisions are equally important. Finalize flooring, wall finish and cabinet style choices before construction begins. Changing these halfway through the project can leave you with surplus materials that no longer suit your plans. Coordination between you, your contractor and suppliers can keep purchasing on track. 2. Keep Existing Materials and Fixtures Where Possible Your home’s existing features might have plenty of life left in them. Keeping functional materials in place reduces the need for new products, which require raw materials and energy to manufacture and deliver. Take a good look at your cabinets, doors, flooring, countertops and plumbing fixtures before deciding what needs replacing. For example, a garage door with a standard torsion spring may last around 10,000 operating cycles. If it still works and its components are in good condition, regular maintenance could extend its useful lifespan. You can refresh outdated features with simple updates. Repaint kitchen cabinets, swap old handles, refinish hardwood floors or replace the bathroom vanity’s faucet. These changes can make familiar features look new again while keeping bulky materials out of the waste pile. Even retaining existing structural elements can prevent substantial demolition waste. 3. Choose Reclaimed and Recycled Building Materials Keeping existing building materials is a good start, but you can make your shopping list even more sustainable by choosing reclaimed and recycled products. They keep existing resources in circulation and reduce the need to extract and process additional raw materials. Look for reclaimed timber, salvaged bricks, recycled glass countertops, recycled metal fixtures and flooring made with recycled content. Architectural salvage yards and secondhand building supply stores are great places to explore. You might even find distinctive pieces that add character to your home, such as an old wooden door or vintage light fixture. Check the condition, safety and suitability of each material before purchasing. Reclaimed wood, for example, should be inspected for rot, pests and damage. You should also make sure recycled products meet the requirements for their intended use. 4. Store Leftover Materials for Future Repairs Extra tiles, flooring planks and paint cans could come in handy long after your renovation is finished. Keeping useful leftovers gives you matching materials for future projects, so you can replace a damaged section without purchasing an entirely new batch. Set aside spare tiles, grout, screws, cabinet handles, paint and flooring pieces. Keep them in their original packaging where possible and label everything clearly. Follow storage instructions carefully because products such as paint and adhesives may need specific temperature conditions. You may also need a place to store these supplies while construction is underway. A portable storage unit can hold renovation materials and other belongings away from busy work areas. It may also protect furniture and household items from dust and debris during renovation, reducing the risk of damage to your belongings. 5. Work With Contractors Who Prioritize Waste Reduction Your contractor has a big influence on how much waste your renovation produces. Their choices around demolition, material ordering and waste disposal can determine whether usable items are salvaged or thrown away. Before hiring someone, ask about their approach to construction waste. Do they separate recyclable materials? Can they carefully remove existing fixtures for reuse? Do they work with local recycling facilities or salvage organizations? These questions can help you understand how they handle unwanted materials. Discuss your waste reduction goals before work begins and agree on practical arrangements for sorting, collecting and disposing of debris. You can also ask contractors to track leftover materials and avoid unnecessary purchases. Clear communication helps everyone work toward the same goal. 6. Donate, Sell or Reuse Items That Are Still in Good Condition Some materials removed during your renovation could be useful in another home or construction project. Donating or selling them gives these items another purpose and reduces the demand for newly manufactured products. The EPA points out that reducing landfill waste can offset the environmental toll of mining raw materials and making new items from scratch. Look for easy-to-remove items such as doors, appliances and fixtures. You can offer them to local charities, secondhand building supply stores or people working on their own renovation projects. Working appliances and attractive light fixtures may also find buyers through online marketplaces. Other leftover materials can serve different purposes. Wood cutoffs can become smaller framing pieces, blocking or garden mulch. You can reuse crushed brick, masonry and concrete as fill, road base or driveway bedding. Even leftover paint can be remixed for use in storage rooms and garages, or used as a primer on another project. Before donating or repurposing the item, ensure its condition is suitable. 7. Reduce Packaging and Avoid Single-Use Supplies Renovation waste doesn’t come exclusively from construction materials. Cardboard boxes, plastic wrapping, protective films and disposable supplies can create another pile of trash before the actual work is finished. Ask suppliers about bulk ordering, minimal packaging and reusable delivery containers. You can also coordinate deliveries so materials arrive in fewer shipments, reducing excess packaging and transportation needs. Save sturdy cardboard boxes and packing materials to organize supplies or protect furniture during construction. For the renovation itself, choose reusable drop cloths, protective coverings and storage containers where practical. Washable cloths can replace disposable plastic sheets for many jobs, while reusable buckets and organizers can serve you throughout the project. Small changes to your purchasing and cleanup habits can prevent a surprising amount of waste. A Renovation That Doesn’t Cost the Earth A beautiful home and a lighter environmental footprint can go hand in hand. With some careful planning, material reuse and smarter waste management, you can make your renovation more sustainable at every stage. You might even find unique materials and creative ways to refresh your space along the way. Make your next home makeover one that looks good and wastes fewer resources. The post Reducing Waste in Renovation Projects Can Be Easy: Just Apply These 7 Practices appeared first on Happy Eco News .

items.descriptionOriginal: The last day of school is a sweet mix of celebration and goodbyes for both students and teachers . One Oklahoma teacher made sure to send her students off knowing they were loved. Former second-grade teacher Melody Munch (who left the classroom in 2023 to create teaching resources full time) shared the touching tribute she gave her class at the end of each school year, which she now helps other teachers recreate . Each year, Munch hosted an “End of Year Awards” ceremony. She presented each student with a personalized award to recognize their skills and gifts, complete with a red carpet (made from butcher paper), music, funky disco lights, and more. View this post on Instagram “I started the Class Awards tradition during my first year of teaching back in 2015. I wanted to end the year in a warm, special way that made each student feel seen and loved,” she tells Upworthy . “The awards were the perfect parting sentiment to celebrate students’ unique gifts. It also made for a fun way to end the last day of school and sent every student out of my classroom with their head held high. Now it’s my joy to share about this tradition and see other teachers around the world put it to use in their own classrooms!” Besides their awards, Munch also sent each student home with a gift bag full of treats. Inside, there was a photo of each student with Mrs. Munch with a personalized farewell letter, a pair of sunglasses, a custom bookmark, and a postcard they can send to tell her about their summer. “So many families tell me their child cherishes this for years to come!” she shared. The “End of Year Awards” explained Munch went all out for the awards show. She set up a red carpet, lighting, music and a projector screen to make the awards feel special. And of course, there was a special microphone. She says she let students vote for their classmates in various categories and made some selections herself. There are more than 60 awards students can earn. View this post on Instagram Awards include: Excellent Encourager, Future Teacher, Remarkable Reader, Most Friendly, Fantastic Friend, Sweet As Pie, Aspiring Author, Animal Lover, Best Dressed, Hard Worker, Clean Up Super Star, Problem Solver, Generous Giver, Caring Classmate, Ms. & Mr. Manners, and more. Then, Munch would hand students the printed certificates. Their names would be displayed on the projector screen, and they’d get to strut on the red carpet to be recognized by their classmates. She would typically hold the awards on the very last day of school, with some exceptions. View this post on Instagram “My sentimental heart loves the closure and celebratory feel this brings,” she wrote on her website . “However, I have had years where multiple students were scheduled to be gone on early vacations on the last day. Thus, in some cases we did our awards on the second to last day of school.” Making students feel seen Munch explained how much the awards meant to her students. “I love this tradition so much! It’s the perfect way to close out the year,” she wrote on Instagram. “It’s so sweet to send students off knowing they are seen and loved. It makes for a great keepsake as well!” She continued, “Students LOVE being called up for their awards. You celebrate each of them for their unique gifts.” “Ending the year is such a bittersweet time. You’ve formed these special bonds with each student, but now it’s time for them to move on. You grieve not getting to be ‘their teacher’ anymore, but you’re also excited for the rest summer brings and the fresh start of the next school year,” she tells Upworthy . “You hope that all the love you’ve poured out over the year will stick with these students wherever they go. Giving each of them an award is just a little way for them to look back and remember how loved they are.” This article originally appeared in June. It has been updated. The post Oklahoma second-grade teacher’s annual ‘awards show’ on last day of school leaves students treasured appeared first on Upworthy .

items.title: Αφού παρακολουθήσαμε πώς ο Boomers αποσύρθηκε «εμπρός», η Gen X αποσύρεται «πίσω»
items.titleOriginal: After watching how Boomers retired ‘forward,’ Gen X is retiring ‘backward’
items.description: Τα περισσότερα Baby Boomers έχουν συνταξιοδοτηθεί εδώ και χρόνια, ενώ τα Gen Xers μόλις πλησιάζουν την εποχή της συνταξιοδότησής τους. Ο Benjamin Brandt είναι Πιστοποιημένος Χρηματοοικονομικός Σχεδιαστής που έχει…
items.descriptionOriginal: Most Baby Boomers have been retired for years now, while Gen Xers are just approaching their retirement era. And according to a finance expert who helps people with retirement planning, Gen X is taking an altogether different approach in determining how they want to spend their golden years . Benjamin Brandt is a Certified Financial Planner who has spent nearly two decades helping people plan for retirement. On his YouTube channel, Even Better Retirement , he says that one big difference between the generations is that Boomers have retired “forward,” while Gen X is retiring “backward.” What it means to retire forward Brandt shares the pattern he’s seeing when he talks to Boomers and Gen Xers about retirement. “When a Baby Boomer sits across from me over Zoom, and I ask them, ‘What are you retiring to?’ You know, ‘Why did you save up all this money? What are your retirement plans?’ I hear a very specific kind of answer,” Brandt explains. “The answers are something along the lines of, ‘I can’t wait to retire so I can finally spend some real time in my garden. I can’t wait to retire because I want to golf three days a week. I want to retire so I can build cabinets in my garage.'” Brandt points out that these are all things the person hasn’t done yet. Boomers want to spend their retirement doing things they always wished they could do. “They retire forward towards the activity that they never got to do and will finally have time for,” Brandt says. They’re basically guessing at what they’re going to enjoy. “That can present a problem,” Brandt points out. “Retiring forward is a bet. It’s a guess. You’re guessing that the thing that you daydreamed about at your desk will still feel good on a random Tuesday morning in retirement when you’ve just got nothing on the calendar. Now, sometimes that guess is right, but sometimes I get that phone call that says, ‘You know, Ben, I’m kind of sick of golf. Is that really all there is to do in retirement?'” The Gen X response: Retire backward instead While Boomers look forward, making guesses about how they’ll want to spend their retirement, Gen X is looking backward. They’re using actionable data about what they enjoyed in the past and planning to return to those things when they retire. “Gen X is retiring back to the thing they used to love when they were younger,” Brandt shares. “I have a client that’s getting the band back together. And I don’t mean that as a figure of speech. I mean an actual band with instruments and amplifiers and a van and a setlist and all those sort of things. In fact, that exact retirement goal has come up more than once or twice in my office. I have another client who’s getting back into skateboarding in retirement. I have another one that’s dusting off his Magic: The Gathering cards and hosting tournaments.” Brandt believes we’re going to see a resurgence of 80s and 90s games and hobbies as Gen X returns to the things they know they’ve enjoyed. He says Gen X’s backward approach is a better way to design a retirement because it’s based on evidence, not a guess. @theretirementnerds The Gen X Retirement Shift No One Saw Coming #socialsecurity #retirementplanning #learnontiktok #retirement #retired ♬ original sound – The Retirement Nerds – The Retirement Nerds Why the two generations differ so much What caused Boomers to have the forward orientation while Gen X looks backward? Brandt says it has to do with the examples each generation has had. Boomers essentially didn’t have an example of retirement the way it looks today. The Silent Generation often had strong pensions, which barely exist today. They had certainty in their monthly income, but no certainty in how long they might be able to enjoy it. “Retirement for many members of the Silent Generation was to retire, then take a cruise, and then die,” says Brandt. “So, the money was more predictable, but the timeline was anything but predictable.” Boomers were the first generation to have what Brandt calls a “full spectrum retirement.” “Many of them had pensions and portfolios and a retirement that could last maybe 20 or 30 years,” he says. “In some cases, in fact, some people have now spent more time in retirement than they spent in total in the workforce. But nobody handed them a playbook because there just wasn’t a playbook that existed.” While Boomers have winged it, Gen X has been watching. And seeing how many of their elders have had mixed results with the forward-guessing approach, they’re going the other way. Additionally, Gen Xers rely mostly on 401(k) plans, which may or may not be enough. According to Fortune , only 14 percent of them have access to a pension. They have less margin of error financially, so they’re being more intentional. Only 18% of Gen X are very confident they will be able to fully retire with a comfortable lifestyle pic.twitter.com/NjMPvZLeo9 — Amy Nixon (@texasrunnerDFW) July 22, 2026 “Generation X is the first generation with a full case study sitting right there in front of them,” Brandt says. “So they are being much more deliberate because they went second, and they are learning in real time from the successes and failures from the previous generation.” The $500 question Brandt asks his clients In his video (as well as his book, “ Retirement Starts Today “), Brandt shares a mental exercise he does with his clients called “$500 in a time machine”: “I hand you $500, and we hop into the DeLorean, and we set the dial back to your 13th birthday,” Brandt says. “Now, you’ve got to spend the money on yourself, and you’ve got to spend it by the end of the day. Those are the only real rules.” At 13, you understand the value of a dollar and have developed enough judgment to weigh your options thoughtfully, but you’re still young enough to have a vivid imagination. “Thirty years in corporate America hasn’t crushed your soul yet,” Brandt says. What do you buy with that $500? Especially if no one is telling you how to spend it and you can be as foolish as you want? Maybe you loved painting when you were 13 but haven’t picked up a brush in decades. Photo credit: Canva “Maybe it’s a mountain bike,” says Brandt. “Maybe it’s a drum kit. Maybe it’s a Dungeon Master’s Guide and some 12-sided dice. Recently, I heard about National Geographic magazines. This retiree loved learning about places that she’d never been, and then that became a desire to explore the planet in retirement.” For Gen X, it’s about youthful interests Thinking about what you would spend a chunk of money on at 13 can help people figure out what they might like to spend their money and time on in retirement. If you still love that thing, you can start making small investments toward it. If you don’t really like it anymore, you just cross it off the list. “Both of those are wins, and both of those are real, accurate, actionable information,” Brandt says. The key is tapping into interests and hobbies that grabbed you in your youth. If they still resonate, your retired self might just want to bring them back. You can follow Brandt at Even Better Retirement on YouTube and find his book here . This article originally appeared in July. It has been updated. The post After watching how Boomers retired ‘forward,’ Gen X is retiring ‘backward’ appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: Between 2007 and 2024, the Coastal Conservation Association of Florida attempted to rebuild the Gulf of Mexico’s ecosystem in an unusual way: dumping over 500,000 tons of recycled oyster and clam shells straight back into the water. These shells were gathered from seafood restaurants (quite literally scraped off plates) as well as seafood plants. So essentially, a massive amount of sinking, rotting garbage was supposedly going to bring the struggling sandy seafloors back to life. Understandably, the idea was met with criticism A pile of oyster shells. Photo credit: Canva Some called it reckless dumping. Others warned it would be detrimental to an already dwindling ecosystem. And for a while, these concerns seemed valid. Even the researchers running this giant experiment had their doubts as no visible progress was initially seen. But beneath the surface, those scrapped shells immediately got to work, even though human eyes couldn’t perceive it. Bacteria began attaching themselves to the discarded shells, creating a biofilm , which is the starting point for pretty much all marine ecosystems on the planet. It’s something scientists still struggle to recreate in a lab. The shells also released calcium as they disintegrated, which produced “microzones,” small, invisible pockets of water with a slightly different chemical makeup that certain underwater organisms need to survive. Not only that, but the dead shells served as a solid foundation upon which living baby oysters could mount and grow. (Previously, due to reef decline, there were only soft surfaces.) The living oysters then filtered the water, keeping harmful algae blooms at bay. All of these things and more helped revive fish, turtle, and dolphin populations to numbers not seen in over two and a half decades. Layer by layer, the ocean floor had rebuilt itself until the results were visibly undeniable. A colorful, thriving reef. Photo credit: Canva Why oyster reefs matter far beyond the shoreline Restoring the balance of these elements is not only critical to marine life, but human life as well. And we’re not just talking about food supply here. A lack of fish means a lack of income for fishermen, and higher prices at seafood restaurants. Dirty waters lead to a decline in tourism. Reefs even provide natural protection during coastal storms. It’s almost like every aspect of our lives is directly affected by the state of our environment. What a concept! How other restoration projects are taking notes The unexpected, overwhelming success of this experiment in Florida captured the attention of coastal engineers and marine biologists across North America, Europe, and Australia. Researchers are actively studying how natural materials can be utilized to rapidly rebuild degraded marine environments globally. Similar shell recycling programs have been deployed in places like Alabama , Texas, Louisiana, California, Mississippi, and the Carolinas, to name a few. It seems like a divine sense of justice that human intervention is the solution to a problem caused by, well…human intervention. Dwindling oyster populations are primarily due to overharvesting, but also to human-caused disasters like the Deepwater Horizon oil spill . While no single project can undo decades of environmental damage, Florida’s success shows that thoughtful restoration can give struggling ecosystems a real chance to recover. In this case, the solution was hiding in plain sight. This article originally appeared in July. It has been updated. The post Florida dumped half a million oyster shells into the Gulf of Mexico. No one expected the results to be this good. appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: Commonplace moments with a stranger can make all the difference in helping someone feel like they belong. You’re walking through the farmers market with a screaming toddler tucked under your arm football style. You’re tired, you’re leaving without the produce you came for, and you’re embarrassed. You pass by an older woman on the way out, steeling yourself for judgment. Instead, you get a knowing smile and hear, “We’ve all been there. You’re doing great, Mama.” And suddenly, you feel seen. Until recently, these sparks of connection didn’t have a name. Now, thanks to a University of Georgia researcher, they do: evanescent interactions. “What is communicated by these evanescent interactions is essentially, ‘You’ve noticed me. You’ve confirmed my existence. You’ve communicated that I am welcome here, that I belong here, that I have a place here, that I have value,'” says Joseph Hermanowicz, author of the publication and a professor of sociology at the University of Georgia. Hermanowicz defines evanescent interactions as brief moments when “strangers exchange gestures that create a ‘spark’ between them.” An evanescent interaction is more than just an ordinary exchange of pleasantries. These moments consist of brief but meaningful exchanges of mutual understanding and connection. “It’s important to be pleasant and kind to people, particularly in our present times, of course,” Hermanowicz says. “But I think it’s also important to recognize that when we do have a certain deliberateness with communicating with people, we could be accomplishing something very meaningful. We could communicate to people that they are important, that they matter, that we together form a community.” In his earlier research on the causes of undergraduate attrition, Hermanowicz found that evanescent interactions often influenced whether a student stuck it out or dropped out. Former students who dropped out says that a meaningful encounter with someone at the university who showed genuine interest in their well-being might have helped them feel more like they belonged. “In the absence of such contact, they felt alienated and not noticed, which fueled or did not impede a desire to leave,” he says. “So they left. “A lot of people are lonely. These sparks of connection can thwart feelings of not belonging in the various groups and organizations that we are a part of, whether those are friendship groups, work organizations, or society more broadly.” Evanescent interactions are brief, positive, and highly emotionally charged. They’re so ordinary that people may not give them a second thought. But they hold larger significance, Hermanowicz says. “Evanescent interactions are crucial to social life,” he says. “Two people communicating empathy to each other and recognizing each other as important holds extraordinary consequence. It affirms our mutual place in human community.” The article appears in Theory and Society . Source: University of Georgia The post How connecting with strangers can boost the sense of belonging appeared first on Futurity .

items.descriptionOriginal: Νέα προειδοποίηση για τα δημοφιλή φάρμακα αδυνατίσματος και διαβήτη που ανήκουν στην κατηγορία GLP-1 εξέδωσε η αμερικανική Υπηρεσία Τροφίμων και Φαρμάκων (FDA), ζητώντας από τις φαρμακευτικές εταιρείες να προσθέσουν στις συσκευασίες τους ενημέρωση για μια σπάνια πάθηση των ματιών, η οποία μπορεί να προκαλέσει αιφνίδια απώλεια όρασης, ακόμη και μόνιμη τύφλωση . Η προειδοποίηση αφορά φάρμακα όπως τα Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro και Zepbound. Οι κατασκευαστές τους θα πρέπει να ενημερώνουν τους ασθενείς για τη μη αρτηριτιδική πρόσθια ισχαιμική οπτική νευροπάθεια (NAION), μια σπάνια πάθηση που εμφανίζεται όταν διακόπτεται η παροχή αίματος στο οπτικό νεύρο, με αποτέλεσμα να στερείται το απαραίτητο οξυγόνο. Σύμφωνα με την FDA, η πάθηση μπορεί να προκαλέσει ανώδυνη μείωση της όρασης στο ένα μάτι, η οποία σε ορισμένες περιπτώσεις ενδέχεται να είναι μόνιμη. Η αμερικανική υπηρεσία κατέληξε στο συμπέρασμα ότι υπάρχει αυξημένος κίνδυνος εμφάνισης σπάνιων περιστατικών NAION σε άτομα που λαμβάνουν φάρμακα GLP-1, έπειτα από αναλυτική αξιολόγηση αναφορών περιστατικών και άλλων επιστημονικών μελετών. Ωστόσο, η Αμερικανική Ακαδημία Οφθαλμολογίας, σε δήλωσή της στο BBC, υπογράμμισε ότι ο πρόσθετος κίνδυνος φαίνεται μικρός και ότι δεν έχει αποδειχθεί πως τα συγκεκριμένα φάρμακα προκαλούν τη νόσο. «Τα φάρμακα GLP-1 προσφέρουν σημαντικά οφέλη σε ανθρώπους με διαβήτη, παχυσαρκία και καρδιακές παθήσεις. Το μήνυμά μας προς τους ασθενείς είναι απλό: μην διακόπτετε τη φαρμακευτική αγωγή σας χωρίς να συμβουλευτείτε τον γιατρό σας. Εάν παρατηρήσετε ξαφνική και ανώδυνη απώλεια όρασης στο ένα μάτι, απευθυνθείτε άμεσα σε οφθαλμίατρο», ανέφερε η Ακαδημία. Διαβάστε ακόμα Δεν υπάρχει θεραπεία για την αποκατάσταση της όρασης Η NAION αποτελεί την πιο συχνή αιτία οξείας βλάβης του οπτικού νεύρου σε άτομα άνω των 50 ετών, σύμφωνα με την Αμερικανική Ακαδημία Οφθαλμολογίας. Μέχρι σήμερα δεν υπάρχει γνωστή θεραπεία που να μπορεί να αναστρέψει την απώλεια όρασης που προκαλεί η συγκεκριμένη πάθηση. Από την πλευρά της, η Novo Nordisk, παρασκευάστρια εταιρεία του Wegovy, ανέφερε ότι τα διαθέσιμα επιστημονικά δεδομένα δεν αποδεικνύουν σχέση αιτίας και αποτελέσματος μεταξύ των φαρμάκων της και της NAION. «Αναγνωρίζουμε ότι η NAION μπορεί να έχει σοβαρές επιπτώσεις στους ασθενείς και τις οικογένειές τους. Η ασφάλεια των ασθενών αποτελεί κορυφαία προτεραιότητα για τη Novo και συνεχίζουμε να παρακολουθούμε την ασφάλεια των φαρμάκων μας», σημείωσε η εταιρεία. Η FDA επισήμανε ότι η αξιολόγηση των επιστημονικών δεδομένων παρουσιάζει δυσκολίες, καθώς άνθρωποι που λαμβάνουν φάρμακα GLP-1 για την παχυσαρκία ή τον διαβήτη τύπου 2 ενδέχεται να έχουν ήδη άλλους παράγοντες κινδύνου για την εμφάνιση της συγκεκριμένης οφθαλμολογικής πάθησης. Παράλληλα, δεν έχει αποσαφηνιστεί γιατί οι συγκεκριμένοι ασθενείς ενδέχεται να διατρέχουν μεγαλύτερο κίνδυνο. Τι δείχνουν οι ευρωπαϊκές και αμερικανικές μελέτες Τα φάρμακα GLP-1 διαθέτουν ήδη προειδοποιήσεις για άλλες πιθανές ανεπιθύμητες ενέργειες, όπως η παγκρεατίτιδα και οι παθήσεις της χοληδόχου κύστης. Στις συχνότερες παρενέργειες της σεμαγλουτίδης, βασικής δραστικής ουσίας πολλών από αυτά τα σκευάσματα, περιλαμβάνονται η ναυτία, ο έμετος και ο πόνος στην κοιλιά. Πέρυσι, επιτροπή ασφάλειας του Ευρωπαϊκού Οργανισμού Φαρμάκων (EMA) είχε προειδοποιήσει ότι η NAION ενδέχεται να εμφανιστεί σε έως και έναν στους 10.000 ανθρώπους που λαμβάνουν σεμαγλουτίδη. Επιπλέον, αμερικανική μελέτη που δημοσιεύθηκε πριν από δύο χρόνια και εξέτασε 17.000 ασθενείς διαπίστωσε ότι όσοι λάμβαναν σεμαγλουτίδη είχαν τετραπλάσιες πιθανότητες να διαγνωστούν με NAION σε σύγκριση με όσους δεν έπαιρναν το συγκεκριμένο φάρμακο. Ο ένας εκ των συγγραφέων της μελέτης, ο καθηγητής Οφθαλμολογίας της Ιατρικής Σχολής του Χάρβαρντ, Τζόζεφ Ρίτζο, χαρακτήρισε τα ευρήματα σημαντικά, αλλά προκαταρκτικά, επισημαίνοντας ότι απαιτείται περαιτέρω έρευνα σε μεγαλύτερους και πιο αντιπροσωπευτικούς πληθυσμούς, προκειμένου να αποσαφηνιστεί η πιθανή σχέση των φαρμάκων με την οφθαλμολογική πάθηση. Το περιστατικό συνέβη την ώρα που…
items.descriptionOriginal: Αντιμέτωπο με έντονες αντιδράσεις βρέθηκε το beIN Sports στη Γαλλία, μετά από ένα περιστατικό που σημειώθηκε κατά τη διάρκεια της τηλεοπτικής κάλυψης των WTA Finals. Πρωταγωνιστής ήταν ο δημοσιογράφος Ματιέ Σολιέ, ο οποίος ακούστηκε να κάνει ένα ιδιαίτερα προσβλητικό σχόλιο για την Αρίνα Σαμπαλένκα , χωρίς να αντιληφθεί ότι το μικρόφωνό του παρέμενε ανοιχτό. Το περιστατικό συνέβη την ώρα που το κανάλι προέβαλλε ένα βίντεο παρουσίασης της Λευκορωσίδας πρωταθλήτριας. Στα πλάνα, η 28χρονη τενίστρια πόζαρε μπροστά στην κάμερα και έστελνε ένα φιλί, όταν ακούστηκε η φωνή του δημοσιογράφου να λέει στα γαλλικά: «Κοιτάξτε, κοιτάξτε, κοιτάξτε, είναι απαίσια». Ο Σολιέ φαίνεται πως πίστευε ότι βρισκόταν εκτός αέρα, ωστόσο η ατάκα του μεταδόθηκε κανονικά στους τηλεθεατές. Το σχετικό απόσπασμα δεν άργησε να κυκλοφορήσει στα μέσα κοινωνικής δικτύωσης, συγκεντρώνοντας πλήθος επικριτικών σχολίων. «Regarde, elle est horrible!» Un commentateur de beIN SPORTS dérape en plein direct, la direction condamne ses propos https://t.co/vdKXboFW5w https://t.co/z60rObyAEw — Entrevue (@EntrevueFr) November 10, 2026 Η αντίδραση του beIN Sports και η δημόσια απολογία Η υπόθεση πήρε γρήγορα διαστάσεις, με χρήστες των social media να καταδικάζουν τη συμπεριφορά του δημοσιογράφου και να ζητούν εξηγήσεις από το τηλεοπτικό δίκτυο. Διαβάστε ακόμα Ο Φλοράν Ουζού, διευθυντικό στέλεχος του beIN Sports, παρενέβη δημόσια, εκφράζοντας τη λύπη του για όσα ακούστηκαν κατά τη διάρκεια της μετάδοσης. «Λυπάμαι και καταδικάζω απερίφραστα τα σχόλια που έγιναν ζωντανά στον αέρα κατά τη διάρκεια της μετάδοσης των WTA Finals. Οι συγκεκριμένες δηλώσεις δεν αντιπροσωπεύουν τις αξίες του beIN SPORTS», ανέφερε χαρακτηριστικά. Παράλληλα, υπογράμμισε ότι το κανάλι παραμένει προσηλωμένο στην αντιμετώπιση όλων των αθλητών και των συντελεστών των εκπομπών του με σεβασμό. Δεν έχει τοποθετηθεί η Σαμπαλένκα Μέχρι στιγμής, ο Ματιέ Σολιέ δεν έχει προχωρήσει σε δημόσια τοποθέτηση για το περιστατικό, ενώ ούτε η Αρίνα Σαμπαλένκα έχει σχολιάσει την προσβλητική αναφορά. Η Λευκορωσίδα πρωταθλήτρια, η οποία βρίσκεται στο επίκεντρο της διοργάνωσης, συνέχισε κανονικά τις αγωνιστικές της υποχρεώσεις, χωρίς να αναφερθεί δημόσια στο συμβάν. Το περιστατικό, πάντως, άνοιξε ξανά τη συζήτηση γύρω από τα σχόλια που γίνονται εκτός προγραμματισμένης μετάδοσης, αλλά καταλήγουν να ακούγονται ζωντανά, με απρόβλεπτες συνέπειες για όσους βρίσκονται μπροστά στα μικρόφωνα.
